# `tfctl variable import` reference

Import variables from .tfvars files or environment variables into workspaces or variable sets.

## Usage

```shell-session
$ tfctl variable import [TFVARS_FILE] [options]
```

## Description

The `tfctl variable import` command lets you import Terraform variables from `.tfvars` files or environment variables from the tfctl process environment into Workspaces or Variable Sets.

You can import:
- Terraform variables from a `.tfvars` file
- Environment variables from your current shell using the `-e` flag
- Or both simultaneously

By default, the command targets the current workspace (resolved from your profile or local Terraform cloud configuration). Use `--variable-set-name` to target a Variable Set instead.

## Arguments

- `TFVARS_FILE` - (Optional) The `.tfvars` file to import variables from.

## Options

- `--env`, `-e` - Environment variable to import.
  - Optional.
  - Data type: string.
  - Repeatable.
  - Imports the specified environment variable from your current shell.

- `--variable-set-name` - Target Variable Set by name.
  - Optional.
  - Data type: string.
  - When specified, imports variables into the named Variable Set instead of a workspace.

- `--organization` - Organization name.
  - Optional.
  - Data type: string.
  - Defaults to profile or Terraform cloud config context.
  - Required when targeting a Variable Set.

- `--workspace` - Workspace name override.
  - Optional.
  - Data type: string.
  - Defaults to Terraform cloud config context.
  - Overrides the workspace resolved from local configuration.

- `--overwrite` - Update matching existing variables instead of erroring.
  - Optional.
  - Data type: boolean.
  - Default: `false`.
  - When enabled, existing variables with the same key will be updated instead of causing an error.

## Examples

### Import terraform variables from a .tfvars file into the current workspace

```shell-session
$ tfctl variable import variables.tfvars
```

### Import environment variables from the tfctl process into a variable set

```shell-session
$ tfctl variable import -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY --variable-set-name my-variable-set
```

### Import both .tfvars and environment variables

```shell-session
$ tfctl variable import terraform.tfvars -e DATABASE_URL --workspace my-workspace
```

### Import with overwrite enabled

```shell-session
$ tfctl variable import variables.tfvars --overwrite
```

## Notes

- When targeting a workspace, the organization and workspace are automatically resolved from your active profile or local Terraform cloud configuration.
- When targeting a Variable Set, you must specify `--organization` if it's not available in your profile or local configuration.
- The `--overwrite` flag allows updating existing variables. Without it, the command will error if a variable with the same key already exists.
- Environment variables specified with `-e` are read from your current shell environment at the time the command runs.
- Variables from `.tfvars` files are imported as Terraform variables (category: `terraform`).
- Variables from environment variables are imported as environment variables (category: `env`).
